title: Berlin Altbau - FAQ
subtitle: What the word means, how to date your building, and where to find the real year.

items.q: What counts as an Altbau in Berlin?
items.a: In everyday speech, any old building with high ceilings. The **Berlin Mietspiegel 2026** is more precise: it calls flats first ready to move into **until 1918** and **from 1919 to 1949** Altbau. Everything from 1950 on is Neubau in the rent index.

items.q: Why does the build year of my flat matter?
items.a: The rent index places your flat by **build-year band, floor area and residential location**. A rent increase or a rent brake check starts from that line, so a flat from 1910 and one from 1925 are compared with different numbers.

items.q: How can I tell if my building is older than 1914?
items.a: Walk into the courtyard. A **narrow yard closed by a side wing and a back house** is the pre-1914 tenement. Tenement building stopped with the First World War, and the **Bauordnung of 1925** stopped new back buildings for flats.

items.q: Why does my old building have a plain facade?
items.a: Many Berlin facades were **stripped of their stucco**, a first wave in the 1920s and the biggest in the **1950s**, in East and West. If the floor heights and windows match an ornate neighbour, your house is probably just as old.

The large room where the front house meets the side wing: a **through room with usually three doors and one corner window onto the courtyard**. It spread with a pattern book of floor plans from 1862 and ended with the 1925 building code.

items.q: Where can I look up the exact year my Berlin building was built?
items.a: Search the address in the **Denkmaldatenbank**, the city's monument database, if the building is listed; its dates can include later alterations. The **Umweltatlas map of building age** shows the main decade for each block, and the **Bauakte** at the district building office holds the original plans.

items.q: Does the Mietspiegel apply to a flat with a shared toilet on the landing?
items.a: No. The Mietspiegel 2026 says it does **not apply to flats whose toilet is outside the flat**, so those flats are not compared with its table.
